sentences.text:
Author: Sharad Kumar Sharma Bench: Sharad Kumar Sharma  Office Notes, reports,
 orders or proceedings SL.

Date or directions and COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS No  Registrar's order with  Signatures  13.04.2023 WPMS No. 1105 of 2023  Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Sanjay Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioners.
Mr. Suyash Pant, learned Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand.
There happens to be a dispute pertaining to an apportionment of compensation, which is claimed to be payable to the heirs of the deceased tenure holder.
The grievance of the petitioner is that the Competent Authority has already recommended the matter for apportionment to be decided but the no decision has been taken on the same till date.

Since, it relates to a grant of compensation under the National Highway Act, 1956, the Competent Authority, has been defined therein under Section 3(a) of National Highway Act, would be an authority as notified in the official gazette to perform the functions of a Competent Authority.

In view of Sub-Section (4) of Section 3(H) of National Highway Act, if there arises any dispute of apportionment of compensation between co tenure holder, the same has to be decided in accordance with the parameters laid down under Section 3(H)(4) of National Highway Act and not way of filing writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

In that eventuality, the matter is relegated to the Competent Authority to take a decision over the issue in the light of the provisions contained under Section 3(H)(4) of National Highway Act, with regards to the recommendations made by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, pertaining to the apportionment of the claim, as it has been raised by the present petitioners, as recommended by the communication dated 07.12.2022.
It is hope and trusted, that the Competent Authority will take a decision, as expeditiously as possible, but not later than two months from the date of production of the certified copy of this order.

WPMS/1105/2023 on 13 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117778254/
1
Subject to the aforesaid, the writ petition stands disposed of.

(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.) 13.04.2023 PN/-
